clue.text: Judged wrong, wanting me to advertise free

indicators.note: set free, these letters are released from their order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who misjudged a situation wants the speaker to advertise without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like 'without charge' but is the anagram signal: ME TO ADVERTISE, thirteen letters, is rearranged; 'wanting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To overestimate is to judge something wrongly by putting its size or value too high.

clue.text: Psychological problem making Greek A hard to handle

parts.note: Oedipus is the Greek king of Sophocles' tragedy
complex means intricate, difficult to deal with

explanation.surface: A psychological issue making a Greek awkward to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'A' is a link, read as the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's term names a child's unconscious desire for the parent of the opposite sex, a psychological disorder.

clue.text: Little fish always grabs line

indicators.note: grabs means the word for always takes hold of the line letter inside it

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A small fish keeps snatching at the fishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a little fish.

clue.text: Chocolate not brought to the hatch?

definitions.text: Chocolate not brought to the hatch?

parts.words: Chocolate not brought to the hatch?
parts.note: these springtime treats are shaped like what a bird incubates but are made of confectionery, so no chick will ever come out of them

explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate eggs given at a spring festival look like eggs but can never hatch.

clue.text: Council about gold rush

indicators.note: about means the council's name goes around the gold

parts.note: the Council of Trent was the sixteenth-century Catholic church council
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A council is concerned with a gold rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold rush' reads as one phrase but 'rush' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rushing stream of water.

clue.text: Generator is revolutionary, good and so effective internally

indicators.note: internally means the two pieces go inside the revolutionary's name

parts.note: Mao Zedong led the Chinese revolution
net means final, effective, as in net result

explanation.surface: A power generator is radically new, good and therefore effective inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A magneto is a small electrical generator using permanent magnets, as in old engine ignitions.

clue.text: Bikini shown without a charge

indicators.note: without the letter a means it is removed

parts.note: Bikini is a Pacific atoll, site of nuclear tests
taken as written

explanation.surface: A swimsuit displayed without a fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bikini' wants to be the swimsuit; it is the coral island. 'shown' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll is a charge paid to use a road or bridge.

clue.text: One coming out with "Rotter! Cad!""?

indicators.note: coming out suggests the letters emerge in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone blurts insults at a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the anagram of ROTTER CAD: a person who calls someone names is a detractor.
explanation.definitionFit: A detractor disparages others, the sort of critic who would denounce someone as a bounder.

clue.text: The French king wants a corps to have powerful trumpeter

parts.note: Louis was the name of many kings of France
an arm is a branch of the armed forces, such as a corps
strong means powerful

explanation.surface: A French monarch wants an army unit to have a mighty bugler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants' and 'to have' are links; 'corps' gives ARM because an arm of the services is a branch such as a corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Armstrong was the great American jazz trumpeter, famed for his strong playing.

clue.text: Gets into water in short strip

indicators.note: short means the word is cut back by its final letter

parts.note: to divest is to strip, as of clothes or property

explanation.surface: Someone takes a quick swim off a narrow strip of beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strip' looks like a noun (a strip of land) but is the verb DIVEST; 'short' docks its last letter, and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimmer who dives plunges head first and so gets into the water.

clue.text: European, in circles close to his capital, avoiding a titled man

indicators.note: close to places the circles-and-European piece right beside the capital piece
avoiding the letter a means that letter is left out of the capital's name

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia, home of the Lett named just before
taken as written

indicators.note: in puts the European inside the pair of circles

parts.note: two circles look like the letter O twice
a Lett is a Latvian, a European people

explanation.surface: A European, socially close to his country's capital, keeps clear of a member of the nobility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'titled man' suggests a lord, but he is the man in an opera's title. 'his' points back to the Latvian, whose capital supplies the start; 'avoiding' drops its A, and 'close to' sets the circled piece beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto is the title role of Verdi's opera, so he is literally a man who gives the work its title.

clue.text: Was not deterred by cut

parts.note: per means by, as in 'per post'
severed means cut off

explanation.surface: Someone carried on undaunted despite being cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep going in spite of obstacles, refusing to be put off.

clue.text: Demand one is to use apron

parts.note: a tax is a demand for payment
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A person demands that someone wear an apron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apron' suggests kitchen clothing, but at an airport the apron is the paved area where aircraft park and manoeuvre; 'is to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft taxi when they move slowly on the ground, across the airfield apron to and from the runway.

clue.text: Speculator investing nothing in the more exotic? Give it a whirl!

parts.note: a bull is a stock market speculator who expects prices to rise

indicators.note: investing means placing the nothing letter inside the word for more exotic

parts.note: rarer means more exotic, less common
O, a zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A trader puts no money into something unusual and urges us to try it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give it a whirl' sounds like 'try it' but is literal: the instrument is whirled round on a cord. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullroarer is a slat of wood swung round on a string to make a roaring noise.

clue.text: Part of the way, say, pawns can be captured

indicators.note: captured means held inside, so the street abbreviation surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: St, short for street, is a way
e.g., for example, is what 'say' means
chess pawns are men

explanation.surface: A chess note: on part of the route, for instance, pawns may be taken.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture of pawns being taken hides the container signal 'can be captured'; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is one portion or section of a whole.

clue.text: Kentish Town cemeteries full?

definitions.meaning: a town in the county of Kent, south-east England, on the Thames estuary
when burial grounds are full the plots come to a stop, a playful reading of the name

explanation.surface: A town in Kent where burial grounds are at capacity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kentish Town' is also a district of London, which misleads; here it means any town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravesend is a port town in Kent on the south bank of the Thames.

clue.text: Utopian version of spiny plant

indicators.note: a version of the word is a rearranged form of its letters

explanation.surface: An idealised take on a prickly plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Opuntia is the genus of prickly pear cacti, plants covered in spines.

clue.text: Head off to kill soldier with a painful condition

indicators.note: taking the head off means the first letter of the next word is removed

parts.note: to total something, in slang, is to destroy or kill it
GI is an American soldier
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gangster sets out to kill a soldier who has a painful illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like 'set out' but removes the first letter of TOTAL, leaving OTAL; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Otalgia is the medical name for earache, a painful condition of the ear.

clue.text: Nest piled high, left new 22 in a mess

indicators.note: in a mess means the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the answer to 22 down, a police baton

explanation.surface: A heaped-up nest, abandoned as a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthill is a mound heaped up by ants over their nest.

clue.text: One progressive type in these early Fathers

definitions.text: One progressive type in these early Fathers

parts.words: One progressive type in these early Fathers
parts.note: Bunyan's hero makes a Progress, and the early settlers of New England are called Fathers of this same kind

explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim is a traveller on a journey of faith, as in Bunyan's allegory and the founding settlers of Plymouth.

clue.text: How pompous Dickensian got at the peas?

definitions.text: How pompous Dickensian got at the peas?

parts.words: How pompous Dickensian got at the peas?
parts.note: the self-satisfied gentleman of Our Mutual Friend is named as if for cracking open the cases peas grow in

explanation.definitionFit: Mr Podsnap is Dickens's smug, pompous character in Our Mutual Friend.

clue.text: Support; it sounds equal

indicators.note: it sounds signals that the word for equal is said aloud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a peer is an equal

explanation.surface: A support said to be on a level footing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a solid support, such as the pillar holding up an arch or bridge.

clue.text: After move, adult fits nothing in this tiny space?

indicators.note: in places the nothing letter inside the rearranged letters
after a move the letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: O, a zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: After moving house, an adult finds nothing fits in this cramped place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After move' reads as moving house but signals the rearranging of 'adult fits'; 'in' places the nothing letter within the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio flat is a small one-room home, a very compact living space; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Piece of wood I found to be police baton

parts.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood

explanation.surface: A stick of timber turns out to be a truncheon.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathi is a heavy bamboo stick used as a police baton in South Asia.

clue.text: South African unknown to have been on the radio

definitions.meaning: a member of a Bantu people of South Africa

definitions.text: unknown to have been on the radio
definitions.meaning: z is a mathematical unknown, and radio operators spell that letter with this code word

explanation.surface: A South African person not known to have broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zulu are a people of KwaZulu-Natal, and the word is also the radio code for Z.

clue.text: The carrying out of Queen of Hearts' order

definitions.meaning: the performing or carrying out of a plan or duty
in Alice in Wonderland the Queen of Hearts keeps shouting 'Off with his head!', ordering a beheading

explanation.surface: Doing what the Queen of Hearts commands.
explanation.definitionFit: Execution means both performing a task and putting someone to death, the latter being the Queen's constant demand.

clue.text: More than half turned up for bit of nostalgia

indicators.note: more than half keeps only the first five of nine letters of the turned-up word

parts.note: retroussé describes a nose that is turned up at the tip

explanation.surface: Most people showed up for a piece of reminiscence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like 'arrived' but is the French-derived RETROUSSE; keeping more than half of it drops USSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro style deliberately imitates the past, so a retro item is a piece of nostalgia.
